deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a record of observations of the 'Wirkung der Reibungselectricität auf den Stab im magn. Observatorium' [1835], i.e. the effect of frictional (machine) electricity on the suspended magnetometer bar in the Göttingen magnetic observatory. The page is purely observational and reductive. There are no theoretical derivations.

Column 1: the time, 9h29'01.5" to 9h34'51.5" at 7 s spacing, then 9h35'00.5" to 9h42'50" at 10 s spacing.

Column 2: the scale reading x(t) of the swinging bar. The free oscillation is clearly visible. In the first lines, maxima of about 669.2 at 8.5 s and 669.4 at 50.5 s and a minimum of 666.1 at 29.5 s give a period of about 42 s, so the half-period is about 21 s.

Column 3: Gauss's reduction, made to remove the free swing. In modern notation (the formula is my statement of the rule he followed):
  y = (x(t) + x(t + T/2)) / 2, with T/2 ≈ 21 s.
This is the mean of two readings half an oscillation period apart. It cancels the sinusoidal free oscillation to first order and leaves the momentary rest position.
- First series (7 s spacing): the pair is 3 steps apart. For example, (669.1 + 666.3)/2 = 667.7 and (669.2 + 666.1)/2 = 667.65.
- Second series (10 s spacing): the pair is 2 steps apart. For example, (667.0 + 655.0)/2 = 661.0 and (660.3 + 661.0)/2 = 660.65.
- The last entry, 665.8, uses the first reading of the next page: (669.2 + 662.4)/2.

The reduced column shows that the rest position does not drift smoothly. It jumps back and forth between two plateaus about 10 divisions apart, with a full cycle of roughly 85–90 s. The next page lists times about 43 s apart, presumably the instants at which the electric action was reversed or switched.

Column 4 (bracketed numbers): arithmetic means of the flat part of each plateau.
- First series: 671.867, 661.650, 672.250, 661.450, 671.737 (mean of 4 values), 661.800, 670.90.
- Second series: 660.825, 671.250, 660.900, 670.536, 660.125, 670.583, 659.700, 669.95, 658.900, 669.95.

Successive high-minus-low differences are about 9.9–10.8 scale divisions (e.g. 671.867 − 661.650 = 10.22, 672.25 − 661.45 = 10.80). This difference is the measured deflection of the bar produced by the frictional electricity. There is also a slow downward drift of both levels in the second series (highs 671.25 → 669.95, lows 660.83 → 658.90).

All of this is data reduction in the style used for the Göttingen magnetometer. The underlying purpose was presumably to show and measure the galvanometric action of machine electricity on the magnetometer.
errors: First series, line 34'16.5: the entry 663.65 equals (659.0 + 668.3)/2 and is correct. But 661.95 (line 34'09.5) should be (655.1 + 667.8)/2 = 661.45. Also, 671.3 (line 34'30.5) should be (667.8 + 675.8)/2 = 671.8. The two discrepancies cannot both be explained by a single misread of the 16.5 reading (668.8 would fix the first, 666.8 the second). So there is at least one arithmetic or copying slip, or a misreading of 655.1 / 667.8 / 675.8.
Because of this, the plateau mean 661.800 = mean(661.9, 661.55, 661.95) inherits the doubtful 661.95. With 661.45 it would be 661.633.

Second series, plateau mean 670.536: it equals 670 + 3.75/7, i.e. a 7-term mean with total 4693.75. The column values 670.4, 670.9, 671.1, 670.3, 670.35, 670.45, 670.65 sum to 4694.15 (mean 670.593). The blotted 38'20" entry (670.65, apparently overwritten) was most likely 670.25 when the mean was taken. The mean therefore was not updated after the correction, or the correction itself is in error. (675.3 + 666.0)/2 = 670.65 confirms 670.65 as the correct pair mean.
All other pair means and plateau means check exactly.

results.what: Elimination of the free oscillation of a swinging magnetometer by averaging readings taken half a period apart, to obtain the instantaneous equilibrium (rest) position
results.modern_name: Half-period moving average / reduction of an oscillating needle to its rest position (a simple comb filter)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard Gauss–Weber magnetometer practice (Intensitas 1832; Resultate des magnetischen Vereins from 1836)

results.what: Measurement of the deflection (~10 scale divisions) of the magnetometer bar produced by frictional (electrostatic machine) electricity, with alternating/switched application and plateau means
results.modern_name: Galvanometric detection of electrostatic discharge current (identity of frictional and voltaic electricity)
results.usually_credited_to: Faraday 1833 (galvanometer deflection by machine electricity); the Göttingen repetitions with the magnetometer are associated with Gauss and Weber, mid-1830s

deep.surprise_reason: This is a raw observation log with routine reduction (half-period averaging and plateau means) of a kind well documented for Gauss and Weber. The only interest is as an archival record of a 1835 Göttingen experiment on machine electricity, plus a couple of small arithmetic slips.

checkable.asserts: Trivial identity; it reduces to 674.1. (The intended check of the 38'20" entry is (675.3+666.0)/2 = 670.65, which supports 670.65.)

transcription_corrections: Line 31'35.5: the reading is 672.8 (confirmed by both pair means 667.8 and 672.3). The '[?]' can be dropped.
Lines 31'21.5 and 31'28.5: second-column values 662.5 and 667.8 are confirmed arithmetically.
Line 38'20: the second-column value is blotted/overwritten. 670.65 is the correct pair mean, but the plateau mean 670.536 implies an earlier value of 670.25.
The bracket 660,825 covers only the two values 660.65 and 661.0 (lines 20 and 30). The brackets 659,700 and 669,95 (second occurrence) likewise cover two values each.
First line time is 9h29'1''.5. The heading folio number reads '50 4/5' with 50 struck out.
Line 41'0: the '41' appears written over another numeral.
